jordan: Heads-up — Acme (private VPC) opened a ticket: intermittent KMS auth 403s + gaps in audit ingestion after we pushed a traffic-shaping policy to their egress edge. Seen during bursty traffic windows. Ticket: https://support.redwood/example/INC-3421

ops-bot: Alert: egress.conntrack_usage > 85% for acme-prod-edge (last 10m). link: https://infra.redwood/alerts/9876 :warning:

devon: Confirming from customer side: getting `403 KMS:AccessDenied` on retries. App logs also show TLS errors around same timestamps. Example from app log: `2026-03-15T14:18:03Z ERROR kms auth failed: tls: handshake did not complete`

maria: Can you collect a pcap + conntrack dump from the node that NATs their subnet? Also need VPC flow logs for the 14:00-14:30 window. Quick repro commands: 
```
sudo conntrack -L | tail -n 50
sudo cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host kms.redwood.internal and port 443 -w /tmp/kms-shaping.pcap
```
And curl to replicate (from inside their prod subnet):
```
curl -v --resolve kms.redwood.internal:443:10.0.2.5 https://kms.redwood.internal/health
```

neha: FYI the edge team rolled a qdisc-based shaping rule yesterday (HTB burst 10mb). On that box conntrack_max is low (defaults). My hypothesis: conntrack table exhaustion + SYN/SYN-ACK drops cause asymmetric flows and TLS session failures -> KMS client gives up -> service returns 403/failed auth and audit forwarder loses events during resend/backoff. Also MTU fragmentation might cause TCP retransmits under shaping. Check `dmesg` for `nf_conntrack: table full` and `ip6tnl`/`tcp_lro` logs.

sam: Add to that: our KMS HSM client opens short-lived sessions; out-of-order or delayed packets can break the handshake state machine and produce a 403 or `invalid session` on the HSM side. The audit pipeline is best-effort and will drop events if forwarder backlog grows; check forwarder queue sizes: 
```
kubectl -n audit get pods
kubectl logs audit-forwarder-0 | grep backlog
```

auditsvc-bot: ingest.metrics: window=2026-03-15T14:00:00Z-14:30:00Z, latency_p50=18s, latency_p95=92s, dropped_events=2763, forwarder_backlog_peak=950 :chart_with_upwards_trend:

maria: Action items: (1) @neha — please increase `nf_conntrack_max` to 524288 on the acme edge and remove/soften the burst parameter for a few hours to validate. (2) @devon — can they schedule a short maintenance window to run tcpdump and provide pcap + `conntrack -L` output? (3) @sam — validate KMS HSM logs for handshake failures and correlate by client IPs (use SNAT IPs from conntrack dump).

neha: I can do one: bumping nf_conntrack_max and changing qdisc to `tbf` with conservative burst. Will push a canary in 15m and report. Also opened NAT translations log for 14:05-14:20.

devon: Will coordinate maintenance. Customer gave permission for a 20m window tomorrow 02:00 UTC. I'll request pcap + `conntrack -L` and the app team will run the `curl` and `openssl s_client` commands you suggested.

sam: For repro, run an `openssl` handshake with verbose to capture TLS handshake messages: 
```
openssl s_client -connect kms.redwood.internal:443 -servername kms.redwood.internal -msg -tlsextdebug
```
Collect pcap in parallel and grep for retransmits: `tcpdump -nr capture.pcap 'tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-syn|tcp-fin) != 0'`

maria: Also need to know audit retention window for this customer (they're on 30d+) — if we have gaps we may need to backfill from forwarder logs once stable. @auditsvc-bot can you dump the forwarder indices for acme-prod for that timeframe?

auditsvc-bot: forwarder.indices lookup: acme-prod: indices available 2026-03-01 -> 2026-03-16. Backfill candidates: 2026-03-15T13:58 -> 2026-03-15T14:35 (partial). Suggest running backfill job after forwarder stabilizes.

jordan: TL;DR: probable root cause = conntrack saturation + shaping-induced packet loss -> TLS/HSM handshake failures -> KMS auth 403s + audit forwarder backlog causing dropped events. Next: neha will patch edge, devon will get pcap+conntrack during maint, sam will correlate HSM logs, maria will own customer comms and backfill plan. Marking P1 until we verify the fix. :thumbsup:

devon: Thanks all — will update ticket with scheduled window and upload artifacts to the support case.

sam: If we see this again after conntrack bump, also check SNAT port exhaustion (ephemeral ports) on NAT gateway: `ss -s` and `cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range`.

maria: I'll loop in compliance for an audit memo once we confirm dropped event counts. Added to the ticket. :lock:

ops-bot: Incident note saved to INC-3421. Participants notified.

jordan: closing thread here; will post summary once we have pcap + results.
